What is capped recall and why is it need.question: What is capped recall and why is it needed?
What is capped recall and why is it need.ground_truth: R_cap@k divides the relevant documents retrieved in the top k by min(k, number of relevant documents) instead of the total, because with more than k relevant documents ordinary recall@k cannot reach 1 and becomes unintuitive.
What is capped recall and why is it need.generated_answer:
Capped recall at $k$ ($R\_cap@k$) is defined as:

$$R\_cap@k= \frac{1}{|Q|} \sum_{i=1}^{|Q|} \frac{|\text{max}_k(A_i) \cap A^\star_i|}{\text{min}(k,|A^\star_i|)}$$

where $Q$ is the set of queries, $A^\star_i$ is the set of relevant documents for the $i$-th query, and $A_i$ is a scored list of documents provided by the model from which the top $k$ are extracted [407, 409]. The difference between capped recall and the original recall lies within the denominator, where the minimum of $k$ and $|A^\star_i|$ is computed instead of just $|A^\star_i|$ [409]. 

Capped recall is needed because measuring standard recall can be quite low and unintuitive when a high number of relevant documents (greater than $k$) are present within a dataset [408, 409]. For instance, if a dataset has 500 relevant documents for a query, retrieving all of them would only produce a maximum $R@100$ score of $0.2$ [408]. Capping the recall score at $k$ is used to avoid this issue [409].
